transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (EdgeStream Head Partnerships), Tom Rivera (EdgeStream Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (EdgeStream PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick sync to align on marketplace listing and RA for joint solution. Confirm infra constraints, security requirements, and POC scope.

[00:00] Ava Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, hopefully the time works. Quick roll-call, I'll kick off with agenda—marketplace listing, reference arch, and PoC scoping. Marco's gonna lead the infra bits.

[00:19] Lena Patel (EdgeStream): Hi hi, thanks Ava, yeah this slot is good. We have a couple of product questions but overall eager to get the listing in the marketplace and talk about the joint solution.

[00:35] Marco Diaz (Redwood-SE): Cool, I'll jump in on the technical side. First high-level, Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments (V P C / on prem). For marketplace listings we generally recommend XXX offering with a quick onboarding flow.

[00:50] Tom Rivera (EdgeStream): Quick clarifying q, when you say private, do you mean full control plane local or just VPC peering to your control plane? We have some regulatory customers that need more isolation.

[01:05] Marco Diaz (Redwood-SE): Good q. We have two flavors: a VPC-peered private offering where the control plane is managed but network traffic is peered, and an on-prem package for air-gapped or fully-managed on-prem. For most partners listing in marketplace, we suggest starting with the peered option then move to on-prem for regulated customers.

[01:38] Priya Singh (EdgeStream-PM): Can you call out what info you need for the marketplace listing? We want to avoid back-and-forth and have the partners team fill the form quickly.

[01:50] Ava Chen (Redwood-AE): Yeah, we'll send a draft. Typical items: product description, pricing tiers (hosted/dedicated/private), expected SLAs, reference architecture diagram, integration instructions for SSO (S A M L) and KMS, and marketing assets. We'll attach a checklist after this call.

[02:12] Lena: Great—also curious about billing model in marketplace, is it usage-based through Redwood or do we bill customers and Redwood invoices EdgeStream?

[02:28] Marco: There are two common patterns: direct listing where Redwood handles the runtime and billing is usage-based to the customer, or a co-bill where EdgeStream procures reserved capacity and bills end customers. For marketplace we usually recommend the first for faster time-to-value. The partnership team can tailor enterprise contracts later.

[02:51] Tom: Ok noted. On the RA, we have some constraints: our customers require private subnets, strict egress controls (no internet outbound except to specific endpoints), and we need to use our K M S for key management. How does Redwood handle customer-managed KMS and audit logs?

[03:10] Marco: We support customer K M S integrations for private deployments and can deliver audit logs to your SIEM. For hosted, we can provide enhanced audit logs and retention, but customer-managed K M S is typically a private/dedicated feature. We'll document exact steps in the RA.

[03:35] Lena: Do you have a reference diagram we can share with our engineering team?

[03:42] Marco: Not yet for EdgeStream-specific flow, but I'll draft one. I'll include peering, NAT/egress, SSO flow (SAML), and recommended instance types and quantization notes. We'll attach it to the marketplace listing draft. (link: https://redwood.internal/ra-drafts/edges-2025-08)

[04:05] Priya: On SSO, our customers use Okta mostly; are there any gotchas?

[04:13] Ava: Okta SAML is supported. One note: for private control planes, you might map IdP groups to RBAC in the console—we'll include instructions. Sometimes the SAML audience or assertion format needs tweaking, but it's standard.

[04:35] Tom: About throughput—some customers expect sustained QPS; what's the recommended deployment for high throughput and low latency?

[04:46] Marco: For sustained high QPS and strict latency SLOs, dedicated GPU pools (reserved) are best. We can size pools based on expected concurrency and tokens per request. Our optimize tooling also suggests batching/kv caching to reduce cost. For spiky workloads we recommend dedicated with burst capacity.

[05:20] Lena: How do you present unit economics in the listing? We'll need a simple cost / latency table for enterprise folks.

[05:30] Ava: We'll include a sample cost breakdown: per-token hosted rate, dedicated amortized cost, and a recommended configuration. We can also include a link to a spreadsheet template (drive: /partners/edges/pricing-template.xlsx).

[05:50] Priya: For the PoC, we want to validate latency under our network setup and a couple of benchmark prompts. What do you need from us to run that?

[06:02] Marco: We'll need network config, CIDR blocks for peering, expected QPS, sample prompts + sequence lengths, and any compliance constraints. If you can share a short prompt set and a baseline latency target (e.g., p95 < 250ms), we can run a short benchmark on dedicated and hosted routes.

[06:25] Tom: One more infra nit: we use strict egress - can Redwood support egress restrictions to only allow specific AWS endpoints?

[06:33] Marco: Yes, in private deployments we can lock egress to the minimal set of AWS services. For hosted, we publish the endpoints and IP ranges, but full egress lockdown is easier with private/dedicated where you control the network.

[06:58] Ava: Quick commercial note—marketplace timeline: onboarding + review usually 1-2 weeks for listing draft, 2-3 weeks for security/marketing review. So if we start this week, we can aim for a live listing in late August.

[07:20] Lena: That timing suits our go-to-market push.

[07:30] Priya: Any red flags for our legal / procurement? We have customers asking for SOC 2 and ISO mention.

[07:38] Ava: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we're in process on ISO; we'll share latest compliance docs. For marketplace, we'll include the compliance matrix.

[07:55] Tom: Regarding telemetry—do you send logs to customer SIEM or do you expect customers to pull from a console?

[08:05] Marco: We can push audit logs or provide pull APIs. For private deployments, many partners route logs directly to their SIEM via s3 or Kinesis. We'll detail options in the RA.

[08:30] (brief cross-talk, inaudible)

[08:50] Marco: I'm going to outline the RA now, here's the rough sections: network & peering, auth & SAML, KMS/key mgmt, instance sizing and optimization (quantization notes), fallback policies and canary for rollouts.

[09:05] Tom: On quantization, we use mixed precision for some models—any constraints?

[09:12] Marco: Our runtime supports multiple quantization profiles; we'll recommend an approach per model. For very latency-sensitive endpoints, lower precision and KV caching help. We'll include recommended models and expected perf deltas in the doc.

[09:35] Lena: Do you have any reference customers who listed on marketplace and ran a joint PoC? Any case study we can reference?

[09:45] Ava: We have a couple—we can share anonymized references and a short case study once the listing is live. I'll include that in the assets.

[10:00] Priya: For the PoC success criteria, can we define 3 measurable goals? e.g., p95 latency < X, cost per 1k tokens < Y, and model output quality A/B score > Z.

[10:14] Marco: Yes that's the right approach. We'll propose a template: latency (p50/p95), throughput (QPS sustained), and quality via a small eval prompt set.

[10:32] (short pause)

[10:45] Tom: Security review—we'll need the security questionnaire. Do you have an existing partner security questionnaire?

[10:52] Ava: Yes we have an SSP and a vendor questionnaire. I'll drop a link and our security contact. Expect a 3-5 business day turnaround for most items.

[11:10] Lena: Any blockers from Redwood side for marketplace listing?

[11:15] Ava: No blockers, just need your assets and sample legal language for co-marketing. The main dependencies are RA and security artifacts.

[11:35] Marco: Also to flag: for private deployments there is some lead time (provisioning dedicated capacity) — usually 2-4 weeks depending on sizing. Marketplace can start with hosted listing to shorten time-to-market.

[12:00] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Tom will share network constraints after the call.

[12:10] Tom Rivera (EdgeStream): yes I'll send the network sheet and our CIDR ranges, also any egress allowed endpoints.

[12:20] Ava: Great. I'll summarize next steps here: I'll send the marketplace draft + onboarding checklist, Marco will send RA diagram and perf guidance, Tom sends infra constraints, Priya shares use-cases/prompts. Then schedule PoC scoping.

[12:38] Lena: Quick note—we also want a joint solution name and short blurb for the marketplace listing. We'll work on that and send suggestions.

[12:47] Ava: Lovely. Any final questions?

[12:52] Priya: One tiny question about model variants and fallback—do you auto fallback to smaller models when capacity is tight?

[13:02] Marco: We support routing/fallback policies. For the PoC we'll keep the primary model pinned but demo fallback options (e.g., to cheaper variant) and show impact on latency/cost.

[13:22] Ava: Alright, wrap up: I'll send minutes and the checklist. Marco will upload RA draft to the shared drive. Folks, thanks for the time.

[13:35] (meeting winds down, chatter about calendar invites)

[47:30] End of recording.

References / shared artifacts mentioned: drive: /partners/edges/pricing-template.xlsx, link: https://redwood.internal/ra-drafts/edges-2025-08, security-pack: https://redwood.docs/security/soc2-2025.pdf

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional speaker attribution and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., SAML transcribed as S A M L, KMS as K M S).

- Ava: send marketplace listing draft + onboarding checklist by 2025-08-14
- Marco: produce reference architecture diagram, instance/quantization guidance by 2025-08-19
- Tom: share V P C peering CIDRs, egress rules, and infra constraints by 2025-08-16
- Priya: send prioritized use-cases and sample prompt set by 2025-08-15

Action items reiterated in call.
